prompt:
Role and task instructions:
You are writing a eulogy for your brother, Jason Wilson, who passed away last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center, at age 67.

User request:
You have been entrusted with the honor of delivering a eulogy for Jason Wilson, a beloved brother, friend, and community member. Your task is to write a speech that captures the essence of Jason's life, celebrates his legacy, and provides comfort to the diverse group of mourners gathered to bid him farewell. Jason deceased at age 67, last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center.
Your audience will include family members, friends, colleagues, and acquaintances from Jason's life. They are a mix of various ages and backgrounds, united in their grief and respect for Jason. Your speech should resonate with this diverse group, bringing them together in remembrance and celebration of Jason's life.
Your speech should not only serve as a tribute to Jason's life but also as a source of comfort and healing for those mourning his loss. It should be delivered in a tone that is sincere, respectful, and reflective of the love and admiration felt for Jason.
answer:
Thank you for being here to remember my brother, Jason Wilson, and to support one another.

Jason died last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center. He was 67 years old. Those are difficult words to say, and I know they are difficult to hear. Someone who belongs in our lives is missing, and we are only beginning to understand what that absence will mean.

To me, Jason was my brother. That relationship holds more than I can put into a few minutes: our family’s history, the years we shared, and the quiet understanding that comes from knowing someone as part of your own life. I will miss having him here as we grow older. I will miss the conversations we still might have had. Most simply, I will miss knowing he is there.

But sitting here with all of you, I am reminded of how many people have their own reasons to miss him.

Some of you knew Jason through family. Some knew him as a friend, a colleague, or a member of this community. Some shared many years with him; others came into his life more recently. Each relationship mattered. Each of you knew something of him that someone else may never have seen.

Together, those memories give us a fuller picture of the man we loved.

As we remember Jason, I hope we make room for the ordinary moments. A conversation that stayed with us. A familiar expression. Something he said that still makes us smile. The moments that seemed small when they happened can become the ones we hold most closely.

Please keep sharing those memories. I want to hear them. Our family wants to hear them. In the weeks and months ahead, hearing his name and learning another piece of his story will be a comfort.

There is room today for laughter, too. There is room for tears, for silence, and for the relief of hearing someone say, “I remember that.” We each bring our own grief into this room, and we can give one another space to feel it honestly.

We can also be grateful. Grateful that Jason was part of our lives. Grateful for the affection, friendship, and connection we shared with him. Grateful that, across different ages, backgrounds, and experiences, we have someone in common whom we came here to honor.

In the days ahead, I hope we will continue to look after one another. When someone wants to talk about Jason, let us listen. When a memory comes to mind, let us share it. When one of us finds the day especially hard, let us make that phone call or sit together for a while. Our care for one another can become part of the legacy we carry forward.

Jason, I wish we had more time. There are things I would still like to say, and ordinary days I would gladly share with you again.

I am grateful to be your brother. I am grateful for your place in my life and for the love that has brought everyone here today.

Goodbye, my brother. We love you. We will miss you. And we will keep telling your stories.
